decisions.reason: It is tightly related to the firm's core airfield lighting and control systems business, and with strong in-house R&D the firm is well placed to learn from early market feedback and improve it rather than withdraw it.

An air situation display fits the firm's established airport surveillance and integrated operations capabilities, so its existing knowledge base makes continued commercialization more likely than exit.
The training program builds directly on the firm's installed systems and service activities, which makes it a natural complement that the firm can support and refine using its operational experience.

Although it is close to the firm's existing airfield ground lighting expertise, it appeared less prominently than other launches and as a narrower training offer it has a somewhat higher chance of being discontinued or folded into broader services.

Airport collaboration software is highly consistent with the firm's strategic move toward integrated, intelligent and data-driven airport operations, giving management strong incentives and sufficient absorptive capacity to retain it.

The multilateration surveillance system is technologically demanding but still closely connected to the firm's established airport surveillance domain, and the firm's own R&D supports ongoing learning and market commitment.
